_comment: Universal limitations shown in the LIMITATIONS tab. Per-analog limitations are generated by the pipeline from feature similarities.

moon.title: Gravity
moon.text: The Moon has 0.16 g. Nothing on Earth reproduces it outdoors. Walking, digging, dust flight and landing loads all behave differently.

moon.title: Hard vacuum
moon.text: The Moon has only an exosphere, ~10¹⁵ times thinner than Earth's air. Only vacuum chambers copy this, not field sites.

moon.title: Radiation
moon.text: No global magnetic field or atmosphere: solar wind, cosmic rays and micrometeoroids reach the surface. Earth's field and air block them.

moon.title: PSR temperatures
moon.text: Permanently shadowed regions stay below ~100 K (some ~40 K). No place on Earth gets this cold, so EarthTwin matches 'relative cold', not absolute temperature.

moon.title: Light
moon.text: At the lunar south pole the Sun stays within a few degrees of the horizon all year. High-latitude Earth sites give low sun and long shadows only part of the year; the polar night/day cycle is different.

moon.title: Regolith and dust
moon.text: Lunar regolith is sharp, glassy, electrostatically charged dust with no weathering. Earth soils are weathered and wet. Volcanic ash is the closest natural match.

moon.title: Rock type
moon.text: Lunar highlands are anorthosite. Earth has anorthosite massifs (e.g. Nain, Adirondacks), but they are weathered and glaciated.

mars.title: Atmosphere and pressure
mars.text: Mars air is ~95% CO₂ at under 1% of Earth's sea-level pressure. Helicopter lift, dust lifting and heat loss are very different. No Earth site reproduces this.

mars.title: Gravity
mars.text: Mars has 0.38 g. Earth tests over-load landing gear and rotor lift requirements.

mars.title: Radiation
mars.text: Mars has no global magnetic field and thin air: surface radiation is far higher than on Earth.

mars.title: Ground ice
mars.text: Earth permafrost and buried glaciers are good structural analogs for Martian ground ice, but they are warmer, contain liquid water near 0 °C and have living microbes.

mars.title: Temperature
mars.text: Mid-latitude Mars is far colder on average and swings more between day and night than any Earth candidate.

mars.title: Slope is screened at ~200 m, not 1–5 m
mars.text: SkyFall's slope limits are set at 100 m (<5°–15°, still TBD by NASA) and at 1–5 m (<15°); the 1–5 m limit needs HiRISE or CTX DTMs that cover only small areas. EarthTwin measures slope on a 200 m grid on BOTH sides (Mars HRSC-MOLA blended DEM; Earth DEM resampled to 200 m). This is coarse-scale screening, not a landing-safety proof: a site that passes at 200 m can still be too steep or rocky at 1–5 m. No HiRISE DTM covering AP-105 was found in this check (the nearest listed DTM is ~4° away), so there is no fine-scale cross-check yet.

mars.title: Thermal inertia and rock cover are proxies on Earth
mars.text: No Earth dataset measures thermal inertia (J m⁻² K⁻¹ s⁻½) or rock cover (%) the way Mars orbiters do. Earth has only proxies, such as apparent thermal inertia (K⁻¹) and DEM texture. They are shown as context and never scored, and the SkyFall filters for both are not applied to Earth sites.

mars.title: Landing site not selected yet
mars.text: NASA has not selected the SkyFall landing site; AP-105 is only a design reference. The first Landing Site Workshop is virtual, 9–10 Feb 2027 (SkyFall Mission Information Package).

method.title: Similarity, not accuracy
method.text: There is no ground truth for the Moon or Mars, so the Similarity Score cannot be checked against 'correct' answers. It says how close the chosen features are, under the chosen weights.

method.title: Proxies on the Earth side
method.text: Rock cover: no Earth dataset gives rock abundance in %, so Earth rock cover is left empty (not scored) and the SkyFall rock-cover filter is not applied to Earth. Thermal inertia: Earth has only apparent thermal inertia, ATI = (1 − albedo)/(day − night temperature), in K⁻¹. It is a different variable and unit from Mars thermal inertia (J m⁻² K⁻¹ s⁻½), so it is shown as context and never scored; the SkyFall thermal-inertia filter is not applied to Earth. Soil and rock type: Earth soil and geological map classes are mapped to the planetary categories with provisional rules (pipeline/context_rules.json); classes with no equivalent stay empty.

method.title: Different scales
method.text: Each comparison uses the same grid on both sides: 240 m for Artemis IV (LOLA ↔ Earth DEM resampled to 240 m) and 200 m for SkyFall (HRSC-MOLA ↔ Earth DEM resampled to 200 m). Both describe regional terrain only. Landing-scale slopes (1–5 m) and boulders are not seen at these scales.

method.title: Missing data
method.text: When a value is missing on either side, that feature is left out and the remaining weights are renormalised. This is shown on every result; it is not a guess.

method.title: Weights and scales are team choices
method.text: The category weights and similarity scales are provisional. The sensitivity check shows how much the ranking depends on them.

method.title: Target sites are not final
method.text: Artemis IV regions come from NASA's Oct 2024 list (marked VERIFY). SkyFall's landing site is not selected; AP-105 is only a design reference.

method.title: Permafrost and ground ice are modelled
method.text: Earth ground ice comes from the ESA CCI Permafrost v5 model (1 km, 2023), driven by NASA MODIS temperatures, not from boreholes. Active-layer thickness is used as the depth to ice, but dry permafrost can be ice-poor below it. Massive ice (yedoma, buried glacier ice) is not mapped, so no site reaches level 3 without a cited field study. The NASA/NSIDC permafrost map (GGD318) needs an Earthdata login and has not been used to cross-check yet. All ice values are marked VERIFY.

method.title: Logistics uses non-NASA data and ignores communications
method.text: The access index uses OurAirports and OpenStreetMap (third-party), because NASA SEDAC gROADS and VIIRS Black Marble need a login. It measures access only. Communications, permits (e.g. the Antarctic Treaty) and safety are not included.

method.title: Coordinates
method.text: Each Earth position was checked against USGS GNIS, the Smithsonian GVP or Wikidata (see Sources → Coordinate check). Three sites have no reference yet. Regions (Mojave, Qaidam, Dry Valleys) are represented by one point, and two points sit on lakes (Tso Kar, Lonar), which affects their terrain and temperature values.
